transformation: Three staged red bridge spans, reversible yellow ramp pillars and a primed blue contact spring become independently drifting support geometry. An inertial motor courier must reach and compress the spring, then commit an aimed ballistic impulse into a moving curved delivery bay. Wheels cannot steer after release. Recent motion traces and a rolling six-second actuator/wind plan expose the outcome-affecting evolution.
license_note: Source mechanics only. No Q.U.B.E. code, levels, characters, art, sound or media bundled.
implementation_boundary: Motion seeds and geometry needed for local render/physics ship to the browser. This is an explicitly screenshot-only task and static play is inspectable. Grading replays primitive control events independently.
observation_revision: The original charts/traces remain. Passive contact instruments show complete physical coordinates, velocity, control latches and spring/bay/wind segment anchors; no seed, suggested aim or interception is displayed.

revision_history.observation_revision: Separate labelled raw-position and acceleration charts; no recommended aim or interception computation. Spring feedback now preserves released/delivered state after flight.

revision_history.change: D1–D3 drift spans are 5800 ms so the initial six-second chart is less effective as a complete traversal plan. Width, authority, wind, flight rules and the D5 profile are preserved.
revision_history.validation: Privileged numerical, raster and exact HTTP native evidence are separately labelled in evidence_docs. Shared paused endpoint/frame findings remain external blockers.

revision_history.change: Supply decision-relevant physical measurements during loaded contact while preserving every physical profile, control, collision rule and grader. This repairs the bounded-visible-window evidence gap.
revision_history.validation: New target-focused rendering, replay and static-play checks are recorded separately. Affected native source validation is queued under the existing admission policy; old v4 runs retain their hashes. Shared-runtime findings are separate from construction, under the October 2 clarification. Independent review and human/model calibration remain distinct.
